ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Steph scored $15$ baskets out of $20$ attempts in the first half of a game, and $10$ baskets out of $10$ attempts in the second half. Candace took $12$ attempts in the first half and $18$ attempts in the second. In each half, Steph scored a higher percentage of baskets than Candace. Surprisingly they ended with the same overall percentage of baskets scored. How many more baskets did Candace score in the second half than in the first?

Steph's entries are 15/20 in the first half and 10/10 in the second half. Candace's entries have blank numerators with denominators 12 in the first half and 18 in the second half. Reasoning: Let Candace's made baskets be x in the first half and y in the second half. Steph's overall percentage is (15+10)/(20+10)=25/30. Candace attempted 12+18=30 shots total, and her overall percentage equals Steph's, so x+y=25. Since Steph scored a higher percentage in the first half, x/12<15/20=3/4, so x<9. Since Steph scored a higher percentage in the second half, y/18<10/10=1, so y<18. With integer x+y=25, x<9, and y<18, the only possibility is x=8 and y=17. Therefore Candace scored y-x=17-8=9 more baskets in the second half than in the first.

Steph's overall percentage is (15+10)/(20+10)=25/30, so Candace must also have 25 made baskets out of her 12+18=30 attempts; hence x+y=25. method.method_draft: Work with missed baskets instead of made baskets. From the image/table, Steph's record is 15/20 in the first half and 10/10 in the second, so Steph missed 5 baskets total: 5 in the first half and 0 in the second. Since Candace also took 12+18=30 attempts and had the same overall percentage as Steph, she also must have missed 5 total attempts. Now apply the text condition that Steph's percentage was higher in each half. In the first half, Steph's miss rate was 5/20=1/4, so Candace's miss rate must be greater than 1/4; with 12 attempts this means Candace missed more than 3, so at least 4. In the second half, Steph missed 0/10, so Candace must have missed more than 0, at least 1. These minimum misses already total 5, so Candace missed exactly 4 in the first half and 1 in the second. Thus she made 12-4=8 in the first half and 18-1=17 in the second, for a difference of 17-8=9.
